{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01QNEnGQ8pbvMQ6d81vzkAa7","type":"tool_result","content":"./league/fixture_lineups.csv\n./league/players.csv\n./league/balls.csv\n./league/matches.csv\n./league/venues.csv\n./league/lineups.csv\n./league/meta.json\n./league/fixtures.csv\n./docs/handbook.md\n./engine/model.py\n./engine/public.json\n./engine/__init__.py\n./engine/league_io.py\n./solution/forecast.py\n----\n# League handbook\n\n## The job\n\nThis is a simulated Twenty20 cricket league with ten teams. You have three seasons of ball-by-ball history in `league/` and a list of\nfixtures for the coming season with the announced line-ups. For every fixture, give the probability that the home side wins.\n\nYou deliver a program. It is run on this league and on other leagues of the same kind that you have not seen, so it has to learn\neverything it needs from the league folder it is given.\n\n    python solution/forecast.py --league <folder> --out <file.csv>\n\nThe output file has two columns, `fixture` and `p_home`, with one row per fixture in `<folder>/fixtures.csv`.\n\n## How a forecast is graded\n\nThe league is simulated, so the [REDACTED] probability that the home side wins each fixture is known exactly. Your forecast is graded against\nthat number. No match is played and no result is used, so luck has no part in the grade.\n\nFor a fixture with [REDACTED] probability `p` and forecast `q`, the penalty is `p*ln(p/q) + (1-p)*ln((1-p)/(1-q))`. It is zero when `q = p` and\ngrows quickly when a forecast is confident and wrong. Forecasts are clipped to [0.002, 0.998]. Your regret on a league is the\naverage penalty over its fixtures.\n\nYour regret is compared with that of a reference forecaster. The reference uses only the files you have, the engine you have, and standard\nstatistical practice. It plays each fixture 4,000 times. Your program is run on this league and on seven leagues you have not seen. You pass\nif your regret, summed over all eight leagues, is at most 10 percent above the reference's sum, and the same holds for the seven\nunseen leagues on their own. Simulation noise in your own forecasts counts against you, so play each fixture enough times.\n\nFor orientation, summed over leagues like these a coin flip (0.5 everywhere) has a little under twice the reference's regret. On a single\nleague anything can happen. Some leagues have little to predict, and there the reference itself can be close to the coin flip.\n\n## The files in a league folder\n\n| file | one row per | columns |\n|---|---|---|\n| `balls.csv` | legal ball | `season, match, innings, over, ball, batting_team, bowling_team, venue, batter, bowler, outcome, extra, position, wickets_before, runs_before, target` |\n| `matches.csv` | match | `season, match, week, home, away, venue, toss_winner, batted_first, first_total, second_total, winner` |\n| `lineups.csv` | player in a past match | `match, team, batting_slot, player, bowling_slot` |\n| `players.csv` | player | `player, role, hand, bowling_style` |\n| `venues.csv` | venue | `venue, home_team, pitch` |\n| `fixtures.csv` | fixture to forecast | `fixture, season, home, away, venue` |\n| `fixture_lineups.csv` | player in a fixture | `fixture, team, batting_slot, player, bowling_slot` |\n\n`outcome` is one of `W, 0, 1, 2, 4, 6`. `extra` is 1 when the ball also produced one extra run. `position` is the batter's place in the\norder, from 0. `target` is 0 in the first innings. `bowling_slot` is -1 for players who do not bowl. `engine/league_io.py` reads a folder\ninto the objects the engine uses.\n\n## How a ball works (all of this is public)\n\n`engine/model.py` is the engine, and `engine/public.json` holds its public constants. They are the exact definition; this section\ndescribes them in words.\n\nEvery legal ball has six possible outcomes. Their probabilities come from a sum of effects on the log scale:\n\n1. a profile for the over being bowled (`over_logits`), a shift for the batter's position (`position_vectors`);\n2. the match situation: how many more wickets have fallen than is usual at that over (`wickets_vector`), and in the second innings a\n   constant shift plus the chase pressure, which is the log of the required run rate over the usual rate from that over on, clipped to\n   [-1, 1.2] (`second_innings_vector`, `pressure_vector`, `par_rate`);\n3. the batter's **style** and **quality**, the bowler's **type** and **quality**, and the **conditions**, each a single number that moves\n   the six outcomes along a fixed public direction (`directions`).\n\nOn top of the ball, with a fixed probability one extra run is added (`extras_per_ball`). Batters bat in line-up order. The strike changes\non an odd number of runs and at the end of each over. The five bowlers bowl in rotation, one over each in turn. An innings ends after 120\nlegal balls, ten wickets, or when the target is reached. The toss is a coin flip and the winner always chases. A tied match is settled by\na coin flip.\n\n## What is hidden, and how it is built\n\n* **Batters.** Style does not change. Quality is a fixed talent plus a form component that drifts slowly over months and is pulled back\n  toward zero. A batter's quality can differ a little against pace and against spin. Every player bats, so every player has these values.\n* **Bowlers.** Type is related to the public bowling style and does not change. Quality is talent plus slowly drifting form.\n* **Conditions.** A level for each venue; a league-wide level that moves from season to season and keeps moving; a pitch-on-the-day\n  effect drawn afresh for every match and shared by both innings; dew at some venues, which helps the chase; a small general\n  disadvantage for the side batting second; a lift for batters at their home ground; a personal liking of each batter for each venue;\n  small league-wide effects of batting hand against bowling style and of pitch type on bowling style.\n* There is **no** effect that belongs to one specific batter against one specific bowler.\n* Between seasons about a quarter of the players change teams, and line-ups rotate heavily from match to match.\n\nThe fixtures are played at the start of the next season. Skills are as they stand at that moment, after one more off-season of drift.\n\n## Rules for your program\n\n* Everything it needs must be under `solution/`. The entry point is `solution/forecast.py`. It may import `engine`, which the grader\n  supplies unchanged, and `numpy`, `pandas`, `scipy` and the Python standard library. Do not change anything under `engine/`.\n* It must give the same output every time it is run on the same folder. Fix your random seeds.\n* It has 12 minutes per league on two CPU cores and must not use the network.\n* The engine is yours to use in any way you like, including to test your own method on leagues you simulate yourself.\n\n## Source\n\nCalibration constants derived from data sourced from Cricsheet (cricsheet.org), licensed under the Open Data Commons Attribution License\n(ODC-BY 1.0). Only aggregate constants are included. Players, teams and venues are invented.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"45d9805e-331d-4ee9-bf4a-c5bbdf92e738","uuid":"7d88a2e2-b895-4777-9956-7724a4a04f8e","timestamp":"2026-09-25T04:51:14.557Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"./league/fixture_lineups.csv\n./league/players.csv\n./league/balls.csv\n./league/matches.csv\n./league/venues.csv\n./league/lineups.csv\n./league/meta.json\n./league/fixtures.csv\n./docs/handbook.md\n./engine/model.py\n./engine/public.json\n./engine/__init__.py\n./engine/league_io.py\n./solution/forecast.py\n----\n# League handbook\n\n## The job\n\nThis is a simulated Twenty20 cricket league with ten teams. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Qe57q6Wiu2YAw6mbirr86Z","type":"tool_result","content":"import json\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom pathlib import Path\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\n\n# runs scored by each of the six outcomes, in the order W, 0, 1, 2, 4, 6; a wicket scores nothing\nRUNS = np.array([0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 6])\n# the two bowling styles, as integers so they can index tables\nPACE, SPIN = 0, 1\n\n@dataclass\nclass PlayerTable:\n    # one entry per player in the league, indexed by player id; these are public facts about a player\n    role: np.ndarray\n    hand: np.ndarray # 0 right, 1 left\n    style: np.ndarray # PACE or SPIN; meaningful only for players who bowl\n\n@dataclass\nclass VenueTable:\n    # one entry per ground, indexed by venue id; also public\n    home_team: np.ndarray\n    pitch: np.ndarray # 0 neutral, 1 helps pace, 2 helps spin\n\n@dataclass\nclass Fixture:\n    # one match's line-ups: the eleven and the five bowlers for each side, plus where and when it is played\n    match: int\n    season: int\n    home: int\n    away: int\n    venue: int\n    home_xi: np.ndarray\n    home_bowlers: np.ndarray\n    away_xi: np.ndarray\n    away_bowlers: np.ndarray\n\n@dataclass\nclass History:\n    # everything an AI agent is allowed to see about the past: every ball, every match, the players, the grounds, the line-ups\n    balls: pd.DataFrame\n    matches: pd.DataFrame\n    players: PlayerTable\n    venues: VenueTable\n    played: list = field(default_factory = list) # the Fixture of every past match (who played, who bowled)\n    seasons: int = 0\n\n@dataclass\nclass BattingCard:\n    # what the innings simulator needs about the eleven batters of one side in one match; built by SkillBook.cards\n    style: np.ndarray        \n    quality: np.ndarray      \n    conditions: np.ndarray   # (11, 5): venue affinity, home lift, hand-by-style and pitch effects for each batter-bowler meeting\n\n@dataclass\nclass BowlingCard:\n    # the same for the five bowlers of the other side\n    kind: np.ndarray\n    quality: np.ndarray\n\nclass BallModel:\n    # Public part of a ball. Holds the measured constants and the five directions; adds up the situation. Nothing hidden lives here.\n    def __init__(self, cal):\n        self.cal = cal\n        d = cal.directions\n        # short names for the five unit vectors: batter style, batter quality, bowler type, bowler quality, conditions\n        self.bs = d[\"bat_style\"]\n        self.bq = d[\"bat_quality\"]\n        self.wt = d[\"bowl_type\"]\n        self.wq = d[\"bowl_quality\"]\n        self.c = d[\"conditions\"]\n\n    def pressure(self, target, runs, ball):\n        # chase pressure, the same formula as in the fit: log of the rate still needed over the rate sides usually maange from here.\n        # `ball` counts legal balls from 0 to 119, so (120 - ball) / 6 is the overs left. Clipped so freak situations do not dominate.\n        need = np.clip(target - runs, 1, None) / ((120 - ball) / 6)\n        return np.clip(np.log(need / self.cal.par_rate[ball // 6]), -1.0, 1.2)\n\n    def situation(self, over, position, wickets, chasing, pressure):\n        \"\"\"\n        The public part of the logits: the over, the batting position and the match situation. Works for one ball or a table of balls.\n        \"\"\"\n        # each term is one effect from the fitted model\n        # np.multiply.outer scales a six-vector by one number per ball\n        cal = self.cal\n        z = cal.over_logits[over] + cal.position_vectors[position] + np.multiply.outer(wickets - cal.typical_wickets[over], cal.wickets_vector)\n        return z + np.multiply.outer(chasing, cal.second_innings_vector) + np.multiply.outer(pressure, cal.pressure_vector)\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def shares(z):\n        # six scores become six probabilities; subtracting the row maximum changes nothing and stops exp() overflowing\n        p = np.exp(z - z.max(axis=1, keepdims=True))\n        return p / p.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)\n\n# Innings Simulator\nclass InningsSimulator:\n    # Plays many copies of one innings at once. Every array below would have one entry per copy, so a ball is one vectorized step.\n    def __init__(self, model):\n        self.model = model\n\n    def play(self, batting, bowling, conditions, n, gen, target = None, log = None):\n        \"\"\"\n        Plays n copies of one innings and returns the n totals.\n        `conditions` is a number of one value per copy.\n        \"\"\"\n        m, rows = self.model, np.arange(n)\n        # who is on strike, who is at the other end, and who comes in next, as positions 0 to 10 in batting order\n        striker, partner, next_in = np.zeros(n, int), np.ones(n, int), np.full(n, 2)\n        # wickets lost, runs scored, and whether this copy's innings is still going\n        wickets = np.zeros(n, int)\n        runs = np.zeros(n, int)\n        live = np.ones(n, bool)\n        chasing = 0.0 if target is None else 1.0\n        for ball in range(120):\n            over = ball // 6\n            # five bowlers rotate over by over; a bowler never bowls two overs in a row\n            who = over % 5\n            pressure = 0.0 if target is None else m.pressure(target, runs, ball)\n            # the public part of the six scores, then the hidden numbers of the striker, the bowler and the conditions, each along its direction\n            z = m.situation(over, striker, wickets, np.full(n, chasing), pressure)\n            z = z + np.outer(batting.style[striker], m.bs) + np.outer(batting.quality[striker, who], m.bq)\n            z = z + bowling.kind[who] * m.wt + bowling.quality[who] * m.wq + np.outer(conditions + batting.conditions[striker, who], m.c)\n            p = m.shares(z)\n            # one uniform draw per copy picks the outcome from the cumulative probabilities; the minimum guards against rounding\n            kind = np.minimum((gen.random(n)[:, None] > p.cumsum(axis=1)).sum(axis=1), 5)\n            # an extra run with the measured probability, independent of the bat outcome\n            extra = (gen.random(n) < m.cal.extras_per_ball) & live\n            # optional ball-by-ball record of copy 0, used by the league to write the history files\n            if log is not None and live[0]:\n                log.append((ball, int(striker[0]), who, int(kind[0]), int(extra[0]), int(wickets[0]), int(runs[0])))\n            out = (kind == 0) & live\n            scored = np.where(live & ~out, RUNS[kind], 0)\n            runs += scored + extra\n            wickets += out\n            # the next batter replaces a dismissed striker\n            striker = np.where(out, next_in, striker)\n            next_in = next_in + out\n            # the batters cross on an odd number of runs and at the end of an over, but not both\n            swap = (scored % 2 == 1) ^ (ball % 6 == 5)\n            striker, partner = np.where(swap, partner, striker), np.where(swap, striker, partner)\n            # after the tenth wicket the indices would run past the eleven; clamp them, the innings is over anyway\n            striker, partner = np.minimum(striker, 10), np.minimum(partner, 10)\n            # an innings ends at ten wickets, or when a chase reaches its target\n            live &= wickets < 10\n            if target is not None:\n                live &= runs < target\n        return runs\n\nclass SkillBook:\n    \"\"\"Everything the engine needs to know about players and venues. \n    The league owns the [REDACTED] one. A forecaster builds its own.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Per player: style, quality, split (pace-versus-spin gap in quality), kind (bowler type), bowl_quality.\n    # Per venue: level and dew. Per player-venue: affinity. Whole league: home lift, era (season level), day spread, wear.\n    # Two small public-structure tables: type_table [hand][bowling style] and pitch_table [bowling style][pitch type].\n\n    def __init__(self, players, venues, style, quality, split, kind, bowl_quality, type_table, pitch_table, venue_level, venue_dew, affinity, home_lift, era, day_sd, wear):\n        self.players, self.venues = players, venues\n        self.style, self.quality, self.split, self.kind, self.bowl_quality = style, quality, split, kind, bowl_quality\n        self.type_table, self.pitch_table = np.asarray(type_table), np.asarray(pitch_table)\n        self.venue_level, self.venue_dew, self.affinity = venue_level, venue_dew, affinity\n        self.home_lift, self.era, self.day_sd, self.wear = home_lift, era, day_sd, wear\n\n    def cards(self, xi, team, bowlers, venue):\n        # builds the two cards for one side batting against five named bowlers at one ground\n        hand, how = self.players.hand[xi], self.players.style[bowlers]\n        # a batter's quality against pace is quality + split/2, against spin quality - split/2\n        sign = np.where(how == PACE, 0.5, -0.5)\n        at_home = self.home_lift if self.venues.home_team[venue] == team else 0.0\n        # the conditions each batter meets against each bowler: liking for the ground, home lift, hand-versus-style, and the pitch's help to that style\n        meeting = (self.affinity[xi, venue] + at_home)[:, None] + self.type_table[hand][:, how] - self.pitch_table[how, self.venues.pitch[venue]][None, :]\n        batting = BattingCard(self.style[xi], self.quality[xi][:, None] + self.split[xi][:, None] * sign[None, :], meeting + self.pair_effect(xi, bowlers))\n        return batting, BowlingCard(self.kind[bowlers], self.bowl_quality[bowlers])\n\n    def pair_effect(self, xi, bowlers):\n        # a forecaster that believes in head-to-head records can override this; the [REDACTED] league has none\n        return 0.0                       # the [REDACTED] league has no effect tied to one specific batter-bowler pair\n\n    def shift(self, venue, chasing):\n        # the conditions shared by every ball of an innings: the ground's level, the season level, and in a chase the dew minus the wear\n        return self.venue_level[venue] + self.era + ((self.venue_dew[venue] - self.wear) if chasing else 0.0)\n\n\nclass MatchSimulator:\n    def __init__(self, model):\n        self.innings = InningsSimulator(model)\n\n    def win_probability(self, book, fixture, n, gen):\n        \"\"\"\n        P(home side wins). \n        The toss is a coin flip and the winner always chases. \n        A tie is settled by a coin flip.\n        \"\"\"\n        f = fixture\n        xi, five = {f.home: f.home_xi, f.away: f.away_xi}, {f.home: f.home_bowlers, f.away: f.away_bowlers}\n        total = 0.0\n        # both orders of batting are played, each with weight one half, because the toss decides who chases\n        for first, second in ((f.home, f.away), (f.away, f.home)):\n            day = gen.normal(0.0, book.day_sd, n) if book.day_sd > 0 else np.zeros(n)       # the same pitch for both innings of a copy\n            set_ = self.innings.play(*book.cards(xi[first], first, five[second], f.venue), book.shift(f.venue, False) + day, n, gen)\n            chase = self.innings.play(*book.cards(xi[second], second, five[first], f.venue), book.shift(f.venue, True) + day, n, gen, target=set_ + 1)\n            # the chasing side wins if it passes the total; a tie is worth half\n            second_wins = (chase > set_).mean() + 0.5 * (chase == set_).mean()\n            total += 0.5 * (second_wins if second == f.home else 1 - second_wins)\n        return float(total)\n\n\nclass PublicConstants:\n    \"\"\"\n    The documented structure of a ball: \n        everything in the engine that is not a hidden skill or a hidden condition.\n    \"\"\"\n    # allowed to see about the past: every ball, every match, the players, the grounds, the line-ups\n    balls: pd.DataFrame\n    matches: pd.DataFrame\n    players: PlayerTable\n    venues: VenueTable\n    played: list = field(default_factory = list) # the Fixture of every past match (who played, who bowled)\n    seasons: int = 0\n\n@dataclass\nclass BattingCard:\n    # what the innings simulator needs about the eleven batters of one side in one match; built by SkillBook.cards\n    style: np.ndarray        \n    quality: np.ndarray      \n    conditions: np.ndarray   # (11, 5): venue affinity, home lift, hand-by-style and pitch effects for each batter-bowler meeting\n\n@dataclass\nclass BowlingCard:\n    # the same for the five bowlers of the other side\n    kind: np.ndarray\n    quality: np.ndarray\n\nclass BallModel:\n    # Public part of a ball. Holds the measured constants and the five directions; adds up the situation. Nothing hidden lives here.\n    def __init__(self, cal):\n        self.cal = cal\n        d = cal.directions\n        # short names for the five unit vectors: batter style, batter quality, bowler type, bowler quality, conditions\n        self.bs = d[\"bat_style\"]\n        self.bq = d[\"bat_quality\"]\n        self.wt = d[\"bowl_type\"]\n        self.wq = d[\"bowl_quality\"]\n        self.c = d[\"conditions\"]\n\n    def pressure(self, target, runs, ball):\n        # chase pressure, the same formula as in the fit: log of the rate still needed over the rate sides usually maange from here.\n        # `ball` counts legal balls from 0 to 119, so (120 - ball) / 6 is the overs left. Clipped so freak situations do not dominate.\n        need = np.clip(target - runs, 1, None) / ((120 - ball) / 6)\n        return np.clip(np.log(need / self.cal.par_rate[ball // 6]), -1.0, 1.2)\n\n    def situation(self, over, position, wickets, chasing, pressure):\n        \"\"\"\n        The public part of the logits: the over, the batting position and the match situation. Works for one ball or a table of balls.\n        \"\"\"\n        # each term is one effect from the fitted model\n        # np.multiply.outer scales a six-vector by one number per ball\n        cal = self.cal\n        z = cal.over_logits[over] + cal.position_vectors[position] + np.multiply.outer(wickets - cal.typical_wickets[over], cal.wickets_vector)\n        return z + np.multiply.outer(chasing, cal.second_innings_vector) + np.multiply.outer(pressure, cal.pressure_vector)\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def shares(z):\n        # six scores become six probabilities; subtracting the row maximum changes nothing and stops exp() overflowing\n        p = np.exp(z - z.max(axis=1, keepdims=True))\n        return p / p.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)\n\n# Innings Simulator\nclass InningsSimulator:\n    # Plays many copies of one innings at once. Every array below would have one entry per copy, so a ball is one vectorized step.\n    def __init__(self, model):\n        self.model = model\n\n    def play(self, batting, bowling, conditions, n, gen, target = None, log = None):\n        \"\"\"\n        Plays n copies of one innings and returns the n totals.\n        `conditions` is a number of one value per copy.\n        \"\"\"\n        m, rows = self.model, np.arange(n)\n        # who is on strike, who is at the other end, and who comes in next, as positions 0 to 10 in batting order\n        striker, partner, next_in = np.zeros(n, int), np.ones(n, int), np.full(n, 2)\n        # wickets lost, runs scored, and whether this copy's innings is still going\n        wickets = np.zeros(n, int)\n        runs = np.zeros(n, int)\n        live = np.ones(n, bool)\n        chasing = 0.0 if target is None else 1.0\n        for ball in range(120):\n            over = ball // 6\n            # five bowlers rotate over by over; a bowler never bowls two overs in a row\n            who = over % 5\n            pressure = 0.0 if target is None else m.pressure(target, runs, ball)\n            # the public part of the six scores, then the hidden numbers of the striker, the bowler and the conditions, each along its direction\n            z = m.situation(over, striker, wickets, np.full(n, chasing), pressure)\n            z = z + np.outer(batting.style[striker], m.bs) + np.outer(batting.quality[striker, who], m.bq)\n            z = z + bowling.kind[who] * m.wt + bowling.quality[who] * m.wq + np.outer(conditions + batting.conditions[striker, who], m.c)\n            p = m.shares(z)\n            # one uniform draw per copy picks the outcome from the cumulative probabilities; the minimum guards against rounding\n            kind = np.minimum((gen.random(n)[:, None] > p.cumsum(axis=1)).sum(axis=1), 5)\n            # an extra run with the measured probability, independent of the bat outcome\n            extra = (gen.random(n) < m.cal.extras_per_ball) & live\n            # optional ball-by-ball record of copy 0, used by the league to write the history files\n            if log is not None and live[0]:\n                log.append((ball, int(striker[0]), who, int(kind[0]), int(extra[0]), int(wickets[0]), int(runs[0])))\n            out = (kind == 0) & live\n            scored = np.where(live & ~out, RUNS[kind], 0)\n            runs += scored + extra\n            wickets += out\n            # the next batter replaces a dismissed striker\n            striker = np.where(out, next_in, striker)\n            next_in = next_in + out\n            # the batters cross on an odd number of runs and at the end of an over, but not both\n            swap = (scored % 2 == 1) ^ (ball % 6 == 5)\n            striker, partner = np.where(swap, partner, striker), np.where(swap, striker, partner)\n            # after the tenth wicket the indices would run past the eleven; clamp them, the innings is over anyway\n            striker, partner = np.minimum(striker, 10), np.minimum(partner, 10)\n            # an innings ends at ten wickets, or when a chase reaches its target\n            live &= wickets < 10\n            if target is not None:\n                live &= runs < target\n        return runs\n\nclass SkillBook:\n    \"\"\"Everything the engine needs to know about players and venues. \n    The league owns the [REDACTED] one. A forecaster builds its own.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Per player: style, quality, split (pace-versus-spin gap in quality), kind (bowler type), bowl_quality.\n    # Per venue: level and dew. Per player-venue: affinity. Whole league: home lift, era (season level), day spread, wear.\n    # Two small public-structure tables: type_table [hand][bowling style] and pitch_table [bowling style][pitch type].\n\n    def __init__(self, players, venues, style, quality, split, kind, bowl_quality, type_table, pitch_table, venue_level, venue_dew, affinity, home_lift, era, day_sd, wear):\n        self.players, self.venues = players, venues\n        self.style, self.quality, self.split, self.kind, self.bowl_quality = style, quality, split, kind, bowl_quality\n        self.type_table, self.pitch_table = np.asarray(type_table), np.asarray(pitch_table)\n        self.venue_level, self.venue_dew, self.affinity = venue_level, venue_dew, affinity\n        self.home_lift, self.era, self.day_sd, self.wear = home_lift, era, day_sd, wear\n\n    def cards(self, xi, team, bowlers, venue):\n        # builds the two cards for one side batting against five named bowlers at one ground\n        hand, how = self.players.hand[xi], self.players.style[bowlers]\n        # a batter's quality against pace is quality + split/2, against spin quality - split/2\n        sign = np.where(how == PACE, 0.5, -0.5)\n        at_home = self.home_lift if self.venues.home_team[venue] == team else 0.0\n        # the conditions each batter meets against each bowler: liking for the ground, home lift, hand-versus-style, and the pitch's help to that style\n        meeting = (self.affinity[xi, venue] + at_home)[:, None] + self.type_table[hand][:, how] - self.pitch_table[how, self.venues.pitch[venue]][None, :]\n        batting = BattingCard(self.style[xi], self.quality[xi][:, None] + self.split[xi][:, None] * sign[None, :], meeting + self.pair_effect(xi, bowlers))\n        return batting, BowlingCard(self.kind[bowlers], self.bowl_quality[bowlers])\n\n    def pair_effect(self, xi, bowlers):\n        # a forecaster that believes in head-to-head records can override this; the [REDACTED] league has none\n        return 0.0                       # the [REDACTED] league has no effect tied to one specific batter-bowler pair\n\n    def shift(self, venue, chasing):\n        # the conditions shared by every ball of an innings: the ground's level, the season level, and in a chase the dew minus the wear\n        return self.venue_level[venue] + self.era + ((self.venue_dew[venue] - self.wear) if chasing else 0.0)\n\n\nclass MatchSimulator:\n    def __init__(self, model):\n        self.innings = InningsSimulator(model)\n\n    def win_probability(self, book, fixture, n, gen):\n        \"\"\"\n        P(home side wins). \n        The toss is a coin flip and the winner always chases. \n        A tie is settled by a coin flip.\n        \"\"\"\n        f = fixture\n        xi, five = {f.home: f.home_xi, f.away: f.away_xi}, {f.home: f.home_bowlers, f.away: f.away_bowlers}\n        total = 0.0\n        # both orders of batting are played, each with weight one half, because the toss decides who chases\n        for first, second in ((f.home, f.away), (f.away, f.home)):\n            day = gen.normal(0.0, book.day_sd, n) if book.day_sd > 0 else np.zeros(n)       # the same pitch for both innings of a copy\n            set_ = self.innings.play(*book.cards(xi[first], first, five[second], f.venue), book.shift(f.venue, False) + day, n, gen)\n            chase = self.innings.play(*book.cards(xi[second], second, five[first], f.venue), book.shift(f.venue, True) + day, n, gen, target=set_ + 1)\n            # the chasing side wins if it passes the total; a tie is worth half\n            second_wins = (chase > set_).mean() + 0.5 * (chase == set_).mean()\n            total += 0.5 * (second_wins if second == f.home else 1 - second_wins)\n        return float(total)\n\n\nclass PublicConstants:\n    \"\"\"\n    The documented structure of a ball: \n        everything in the engine that is not a hidden skill or a hidden condition.\n    \"\"\"\n    # This is what ships to the agent as public.json: the profiles, the situation responses, the directions and the extras rate.\n    # The spreads, the venue spread and the real targets from \"par_rate\")\n\n    def __init__(self, raw):\n        for name in self.FIELDS:\n            setattr(self, name, np.array(raw[name]))\n        self.directions = {k: np.array(v) for k, v in raw[\"directions\"].items()}\n        self.extras_per_ball = raw[\"extras_per_ball\"]\n\n    @classmethod\n    def from_calibration(cls, cal):\n        raw = {name: getattr(cal, name).tolist() for in self.X}\n        self.K = B.size\n        self.onehot = np.zeros((n, 6)); self.onehot[np.arange(n), self.y] = 1.0\n        # default hyperparameters (prior variances); refined by EM\n        self.hyper = dict(style=0.15, split=0.05, kind=0.15, level=0.05, era=0.05, day=0.02, chase=0.05, wear=1.0,\n                          aff=0.01, home=1.0, type=0.01, pitch=0.01)\n        self.Sigma_q = 0.1 * np.eye(S) + 0.1\n        self.Sigma_bq = 0.1 * np.eye(S) + 0.1\n        self.kind_mean = np.zeros(2)  # prior mean of bowler kind by public style\n        self.bowler_style = h.players.style[self.bowlers]\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ prior\n    def _prior(self):\n        \"\"\"Sparse precision matrix and prior mean for the current hyperparameters.\"\"\"\n        B, S = self.B, self.S\n        diag = np.zeros(self.K)\n        for name, var in self.hyper.items():\n            start, size = B.blocks[name]\n            diag[start:start + size] = 1.0 / var\n        Lam = sp.diags(diag).tolil()\n        for name, Sig, count in ((\"q\", self.Sigma_q, self.P), (\"bq\", self.Sigma_bq, self.n_bowl)):\n            start, size = B.blocks[name]\n            inv = np.linalg.inv(Sig)\n            rows = start + np.repeat(np.arange(count) * S, S * S) + np.tile(np.repeat(np.arange(S), S), count)\n            cols = start + np.repeat(np.arange(count) * S, S * S) + np.tile(np.tile(np.arange(S), S), count)\n            blk = sp.coo_matrix((np.tile(inv.ravel(), count), (rows, cols)), shape=(self.K, self.K))\n            Lam = Lam + blk.tolil()\n        mean = np.zeros(self.K)\n        start, size = B.blocks[\"kind\"]\n        mean[start:start + size] = self.kind_mean[self.bowler_style]\n        return Lam.tocsr(), mean\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ likelihood\n    def logits(self, theta):\n        z = self.base.copy()\n        for d, X in self.X.items():\n            z += np.outer(X @ theta, self.dirs[d])\n        return z\n\n    def probs(self, theta):\n        z = self.logits(theta)\n        p = np.exp(z - z.max(axis=1, keepdims=True))\n        return p / p.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)\n\n    def objective(self, theta, Lam, mean):\n        p = self.probs(theta)\n        nll = -np.log(p[np.arange(len(self.y)), self.y] + 1e-300).sum()\n        R = self.onehot - p\n        g = np.zeros(self.K)\n        for d, X in self.X.items():\n            g -= X.T @ (R @ self.dirs[d])\n        dtheta = theta - mean\n        Lt = Lam @ dtheta\n        return nll + 0.5 * dtheta @ Lt, g + Lt\n\n    def fit(self, theta0=None, maxiter=500):\n        Lam, mean = self._prior()\n        x0 = mean.copy() if theta0 is None else theta0\n        res = minimize(self.objective, x0, args=(Lam, mean), jac=True, method=\"L-BFGS-B\", options=dict(maxiter=maxiter, maxcor=30))\n        self.theta = res.x\n        self.Lam, self.mean = Lam, mean\n        return res\n\n    def hessian(self, theta=None):\n        theta = self.theta if theta is None else theta\n        p = self.probs(theta)\n        names = list(self.X)\n        H = self.Lam.toarray()\n        pd_ = {d: p @ self.dirs[d] for d in names}\n        for i, a in enumerate(names):\n            for b_ in names[i:]:\n                w = p @ (self.dirs[a] * self.dirs[b_]) - pd_[a] * pd_[b_]\n                blk = (self.X[a].T @ sp.diags(w) @ self.X[b_]).toarray()\n                H += blk if a == b_ else blk + blk.T\n        return H\n\n    def laplace(self):\n        H = self.hessian()\n        c, low = cho_factor(H, lower=True)\n        self.cov = cho_solve((c, low), np.eye(self.K))\n        self.chol_cov = np.linalg.cholesky(self.cov + 1e-12 * np.eye(self.K))\n        return self.cov\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ accessors\n    def block(self, name, arr=None):\n        arr = self.theta if arr is None else arr\n        start, size = self.B.blocks[name]\n        return arr[start:start + size]\n\n    def block_cov(self, name):\n        start, size = self.B.blocks[name]\n        return self.cov[start:start + size, start:start + size]\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ EM\n    def em_step(self):\n        \"\"\"Update prior variances from posterior second moments (one M step of Laplace-EM).\"\"\"\n        B, S = self.B, self.S\n        var = np.diag(self.cov)\n        new = {}\n        for name in self.hyper:\n            if name in (\"wear\", \"home\"):\n                continue  # single free parameters keep a broad prior\n            start, size = B.blocks[name]\n            th = self.theta[start:start + size] - self.mean[start:start + size]\n            new[name] = float(np.mean(th ** 2 + var[start:start + size]))\n        self.hyper.update(new)\n        for name, count, attr in ((\"q\", self.P, \"Sigma_q\"), (\"bq\", self.n_bowl, \"Sigma_bq\")):\n            start, size = B.blocks[name]\n            th = self.theta[start:start + size].reshape(count, S)\n            C = self.cov[start:start + size, start:start + size]\n            Cb = np.array([C[i * S:(i + 1) * S, i * S:(i + 1) * S] for i in range(count)])\n            Sig = (np.einsum(\"is,it->st\", th, th) + Cb.sum(0)) / count\n            setattr(self, attr, Sig)\n        k = self.block(\"kind\")\n        for s in (PACE, SPIN):\n            sel = self.bowler_style == s\n            self.kind_mean[s] = k[sel].mean() if sel.any() else 0.0\n        start, size = B.blocks[\"kind\"]\n        th = k - self.kind_mean[self.bowler_style]\n        self.hyper[\"kind\"] = float(np.mean(th ** 2 + var[start:start + size]))\n        return dict(self.hyper, Sigma_q=self.Sigma_q.copy(), Sigma_bq=self.Sigma_bq.copy(), kind_mean=self.kind_mean.copy())\n\n\ndef ar_structure(Sig):\n    \"\"\"Fit talent variance, form variance and season-to-season correlation to a season covariance matrix.\"\"\"\n    S = Sig.shape[0]\n    lags = {}\n    for i in range(S):\n        for j in range(S):\n            lags.setdefault(abs(i - j), []).append(Sig[i, j])\n    c = np.array([np.mean(lags[l]) for l in range(S)])\n    best = None\n    for rho in np.linspace(0.0, 0.999, 400):\n        A = np.stack([np.ones(S), rho ** np.arange(S)], 1)\n        coef, *_ = self.bform = g.normal(0, hp['bform_sd'], P)\n        self.level = g.normal(0, hp['level_sd'], V)\n        self.dew = np.where(g.random(V) < hp['dew_p'], np.abs(g.normal(0, hp['dew_sd'], V)), 0.0)\n        self.aff = g.normal(0, hp['aff_sd'], (P, V))\n        self.era = 0.0\n        self.type_table = g.normal(0, hp['type_sd'], (2, 2))\n        pt = np.zeros((2, 3)); ar = roster[self.players.role[roster] == 1]; bw = roster[self.players.role[roster] == 2]\n        l = g.integers(3, 6); j = g.integers(max(1, 5 - l), 4); k = 11 - l - j\n        if k > 7: k = 7; j = 11 - l - k\n        sb = g.choice(bat, k, replace=False); sa = g.choice(ar, j, replace=False); sw = g.choice(bw, l, replace=False)\n        g.shuffle(sb); g.shuffle(sa); g.shuffle(sw)\n        xi = np.concatenate([sb, sa, sw])\n        five = np.concatenate([sw, sa[:5 - l]]); g.shuffle(teams); self.team[movers] = teams\n\n    def play_match(self, season, match, week, home, away, venue, book):\n        g = self.g\n        xi_h, five_h = self.lineup(home); xi_a, five_a = self.lineup(away)\n        toss = home if g.random() < 0.5 else away\n        first = away if toss == home else home\n        second = home if first == away else away\n        xi = {home: xi_h, away: xi_a}; five = {home: five_h, away: five_a}\n        day = g.normal(0, book.day_sd)\n        rows, totals = [], []\n        target = None\n        for inn, (bt, bw) in enumerate(((first, second), (second, first)), 1):\n            log = []\n            b, w = book.cards(xi[bt], bt, five[bw], venue)\n            tot = self.sim.play(b, w, book.shift(venue, inn == 2) + day, 1, g, target=target, log=log)[0]\n            for (ball, striker, who, kind, extra, wk, runs) in log:\n                rows.append((season, match, inn, ball // 6, ball % 6, bt, bw, venue, int(xi[bt][striker]), int(five[bw][who]), kind, extra, striker, wk, runs, 0 if target is None else target))\n            totals.append(int(tot))\n            target = tot + 1\n        if totals[1] > totals[0]: winner = second\n        elif totals[1] < totals[0]: winner = first\n        else: winner = first if g.random() < 0.5 else second\n        fx = Fixture(match, season, home, away, venue, xi_h, five_h, xi_a, five_a)\n        return rows, (season, match, week, home, away, venue, toss, first, totals[0], totals[1], winner), fx\n\n    def run(self, out):\n        hp = self.hp\n        self.build_players()\n        balls, matches, played = [], [], []\n        m = 0\n        for s in range(hp['seasons']):\n            if s > 0:\n                self.reshuffle();  a = ar_structure(Sig)\n            # covariance of season-level qualities with the fixture-time quality, under talent + AR(1) form\n            gaps = (S - np.arange(S)) - 1 + kappa  # seasons between each past season's middle and the fixture\n            c = a[\"tau2\"] + a[\"f2\"] * a[\"rho\"] ** gaps\n            Sinv = np.linalg.inv(Sig)\n            A = c @ Sinv\n            cond_var = max(a[\"tau2\"] + a[\"f2\"] - c @ Sinv @ c, 1e-8)\n            self.ar[name] = (A, cond_var, a)\n        self.era_step_var = F.hyper[\"era\"] if era_step_var is None else era_step_var\n\n    def draw(self, fixture, n, gen):\n        F, S, h = self.F, self.F.S, self.F.h\n        f = fixture\n        players = np.concatenate([f.home_xi, f.away_xi])\n        bowlers = np.concatenate([f.home_bowlers, f.away_bowlers])\n        v = f.venue\n        B = F.B\n        idx = [B.index(\"style\", players), B.index(\"q\", (players[:, None] * S + np.arange(S)).ravel()), B.index(\"split\", players),\n               B.index(\"level\", [v]), B.index(\"chase\", [v]), B.index(\"era\", [S - 1]), B.index(\"wear\", [0]), B.index(\"home\", [0]),\n               B.index(\"aff\", players * F.V + v), B.index(\"type\", np.arange(4)), B.index(\"pitch\", np.arange(6))]\n        known = np.isin(bowlers, F.bowlers)\n        bidx = np.searchsorted(F.bowlers, bowlers[known])\n        idx += [B.index(\"kind\", bidx), B.index(\"bq\", (bidx[:, None] * S + np.arange(S)).ravel())]\n        sizes = [len(i) for i in idx]\n        allidx = np.concatenate(idx)\n        mean = F.theta[allidx]\n        C = F.cov[np.ix_(allidx, allidx)]\n        L = np.linalg.cholesky(C + 1e-10 * np.eye(len(allidx)))\n        draws = mean[None, :] + gen.standard_normal((n, len(allidx))) @ L.T\n        parts = np.split(draws, np.cumsum(sizes)[:-1], axis=1)\n        (style, q, split, level, chase, era, wear, home, aff, type_, pitch, kind_k, bq_k) = parts\n        np_ = len(players)\n        A, cv, _ = self.ar[\"q\"]\n        q3 = q.reshape(n, np_, S) @ A + np.sqrt(cv) * gen.standard_normal((n, np_))\n        A, cv, _ = self.ar[\"bq\"]\n        nb = len(bowlers)\n        kind = np.empty((n, nb)); bq3 = np.empty((n, nb))\n        kind[:, known] = kind_k\n        bq3[:, known] = bq_k.reshape(n, known.sum(), S) @ A + np.sqrt(cv) * gen.standard_normal((n, known.sum()))\n        if (~known).any():\n            unk = np.where(~known)[0]\n            kind[:, unk] = F.kind_mean[h.players.style[bowlers[unk]]] + np.sqrt(F.hyper[\"kind\"]) * gen.standard_normal((n, len(unk)))\n            _, _, a = self.ar[\"bq\"]\n            bq3[:, unk] = np.sqrt(a[\"tau2\"] + a[\"f2\"]) * gen.standard_normal((n, len(unk)))\n        era3 = era[:, 0] + np.sqrt(self.era_step_var) * gen.standard_normal(n)\n        out = dict(style=style, q=q3, split=split, kind=kind, bq=bq3, level=level[:, 0], chase=chase[:, 0], era=era3, wear=wear[:, 0],\n                   home=home[:, 0], aff=aff, type=type_.reshape(n, 2, 2), pitch=pitch.reshape(n, 2, 3))\n        return out\n\n\nclass Simulator:\n    \"\"\"The engine's innings and match mechanics, with a different skill book in every copy.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, model, history):\n        self.m = model\n        self.h = history\n\n    def innings(self, style, quality, cond, kind, bq, shift, n, gen, target=None):\n        m, rows = self.m, np.arange(n)\n        striker, partner, next_in = np.zeros(n, int), np.ones(n, int), np.full(n, 2)\n        wickets = np.zeros(n, int); runs = np.zeros(n, int); live = np.ones(n, bool)\n        chasing = 0.0 if target is None else 1.0\n        chase_vec = np.full(n, chasing)\n        for ball in range(120):\n            over = ball // 6\n            who = over % 5\n            pressure = 0.0 if target is None else m.pressure(target, runs, ball)\n            z = m.situation(over, striker, wickets, chase_vec, pressure)\n            z = z + np.outer(style[rows, striker], m.bs) + np.outer(quality[rows, striker, who], m.bq)\n            z = z + np.outer(kind[:, who], m.wt) + np.outer(bq[:, who], m.wq) + np.outer(shift + cond[rows, striker, who], m.c)\n            p = m.shares(z)\n            kind_ = np.minimum((gen.random(n)[:, None] > p.cumsum(axis=1)).sum(axis=1), 5)\n            extra = (gen.random(n) < m.cal.extras_per_ball) & live\n            out = (kind_ == 0) & live\n            scored = np.where(live & ~out, RUNS[kind_], 0)\n            runs += scored + extra\n            wickets += out\n            striker = np.where(out, next_in, striker)\n            next_in = next_in + out\n            swap = (scored % 2 == 1) ^ (ball % 6 == 5)\n            striker, partner = np.where(swap, partner, striker), np.where(swap, striker, partner)\n            striker, partner = np.minimum(striker, 10), np.minimum(partner, 10)\n            live &= wickets < 10\n            if target is not None:\n                live &= runs < target\n        return runs\n\n    def cards(self, d, bat_slice, team, bowl_slice, venue, n):\n        \"\"\"Per-copy batting arrays for the eleven in bat_slice against the five bowlers in bowl_slice.\"\"\"\n        h = self.h\n        xi = self.players[bat_slice]; five = self.bowlers[bowl_slice]\n        hand = h.players.hand[xi]; how = h.players.style[five]\n        sign = np.where(how == PACE, 0.5, -0.5)\n        at_home = d[\"home\"] if h.venues.home_team[venue] == team else np.zeros(n)\n        quality = d[\"q\"][:, bat_slice][:, :, None] + d[\"split\"][:, bat_slice][:, :, None] * sign[None, None, :]\n        meeting = (d[\"aff\"][:, bat_slice] + at_home[:, None])[:, :, None] + d[\"type\"][:, hand][:, :, how] - d[\"pitch\"][:, how][:, :, venue_pitch(h, venue)][:, None, :]\n        return d[\"style\"][:, bat_slice], quality, meeting, d[\"kind\"][:, bowl_slice], d[\"bq\"][:, bowl_slice]\n\n    def win_probability(self, d, f, n, gen, day_sd):\n        self.players = np.concatenate([f.home_xi, f.away_xi]); self.bowlers = np.concatenate([f.home_bowlers, f.away_bowlers])\n        sl = {f.home: (slice(0, 11), slice(0, 5)), f.away: (slice(11, 22), slice(5, 10))}\n        base = d[\"level\"] + d[\"era\"]\n        chase_shift = d[\"chase\"] - d[\"wear\"]\n        total = 0.0\n        for first, second in ((f.home, f.away), (f.away, f.home)):\n            day = gen.normal(0.0, day_sd, n)\n            s1, q1, c1, k1, b1 = self.cards(d, sl[first][0], first, sl[second][1], f.venue, n)\n            set_ = self.innings(s1, q1, c1, k1, b1, base + day, n, gen)\n            s2, q2, c2, k2, b2 = self.cards(d, sl[second][0], second, sl[first][1], f.venue, n)\n            chase = self.innings(s2, q2, c2, k2, b2, base + chase_shift + day, n, gen, target=set_ + 1)\n            second_wins = (chase > set_).mean() + 0.5 * (chase == set_).mean()\n            total += 0.5 * (second_wins if second == f.home else 1 - second_wins)\n        return float(total)\n\n\ndef venue_pitch(h, venue):\n    return int(h.venues.pitch[venue])\n\n\ndef fit_league(history, em_iters=5, log=print):\n    F = LeagueFit(history)\n    theta = None\n    for it in range(em_iters + 1):\n        t = time.time()\n        res = F.fit(theta); theta = res.x\n        F.laplace()\n        if it < em_iters:\n            F.em_step()\n            for k, fl in FLOORS.items():\n                F.hyper[k] = max(F.hyper[k], fl)\n        log(f\"em {it}: obj {res.fun:.1f} nit {res.nit} {time.time() - t:.1f}s hyper \" + \" \".join(f\"{k}={v:.4f}\" for k, v in F.hyper.items()))\n    return F\n\n\ndef forecast(folder, n=8000, seed=12345, em_iters=5, log=print, posterior=True):\n    history, fixtures = load_league(folder)\n    F = fit_league(history, em_iters, log)\n    model = load_public_model()\n    post = Posterior(F)\n    sim = Simulator(model, history)\n    day_sd = float(np.sqrt(F.hyper[\"day\"]))\n    out = []\n    for i, f in enumerate(fixtures):\n        gen = np.random.default_rng(seed + i)\n        d = post.draw(f, n, gen)\n        if not posterior:\n            d = {k: np.repeat(np.mean(v, axis=0, keepdims=True), n, axis=0) for k, v in d.items()}\n        p = sim.win_probability(d, f, n, gen, day_sd)\n        out.append((f.match, p))\n    return pd.DataFrame(out, columns=[\"fixture\", \"p_home\"]), F, post\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    parser.add_argument(\"--league\", required=True)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--out\", required=True)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--n\", type=int, default=8000)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--em\", type=int, default=5)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--map\", action=\"store_[REDACTED]\", help=\"simulate at the posterior mean instead of drawing\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--quiet\", action=\"store_[REDACTED]\")\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n    t0 = time.time()\n    log = (lambda *a: None) if args.quiet else (lambda *a: print(*a, file=sys.stderr))\n    df, F, post = forecast(args.league, n=args.n, em_iters=args.em, log=log, posterior=not args.map)\n    df[\"p_home\"] = df.p_home.clip(0.002, 0.998)\n t\n        final = it == em_iters or (deadline is not None and time.time() + 1.5 * last > deadline)\n        if not final:\n            F.em_step()\n            for k, fl in FLOORS.items():\n                F.hyper[k] = max(F.hyper[k], fl)\n        log(f\"em {it}: obj {res.fun:.1f} nit {res.nit} {last:.1f}s hyper \" + \" \".join(f\"{k}={v:.4f}\" for k, v in F.hyper.items())\n            + \" ar \" + \" \".join(f\"{k}={v:.4f}\" for k, v in F.ar.items()))\n        if final:\n            break\n    return F\n\"\"\")\nf = f.replace(\"\"\"def forecast(folder, n=8000, seed=12345, em_iters=5, log=print, posterior=True, prior=None, prior_weight=1.0):\n    history, fixtures = load_league(folder)\n    F = fit_league(history, em_iters, log, prior, prior_weight)\"\"\", \"\"\"def forecast(folder, n=10000, seed=12345, em_iters=12, log=print, posterior=True, prior=None, prior_weight=1.0, budget=420.0):\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Returns (forecast table, fit, posterior). `budget` is wall-clock seconds to reserve for the whole run.\\\"\\\"\\\"\n    t0 = time.time()\n    history, fixtures = load_league(folder)\n    # leave time for simulation: about 3 seconds per fixture at n = 10000 on two cores, reserved generously\n    F = fit_league(history, em_iters, log, prior, prior_weight, deadline=t0 + budget - {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CfPfsJBstHtXKKVDXmPsN","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The forecaster is complete and validated. Here is the recap.\n\n**What I built.** `solution/forecast.py` with `solution/fit.py` replaces the 0.5 starter. It fits the engine's own ball model to the three seasons of history as a multinomial logistic regression, with one scalar per hidden quantity along its public direction: batter style, per-season batter quality, pace/spin split, bowler type, per-season bowler quality, venue level, season level, per-match pitch effect, per-venue chase shift, wear, home lift, affinity, and the two small tables. Prior variances come from Laplace-EM on each league, and season-level quality uses a talent plus AR(1) form structure with the drift rate pooled across batters and bowlers. Each fixture is then played 10,000 times per batting order with the engine's innings mechanics, where every simulated copy uses its own draw of the hidden numbers from the posterior, extrapolated one off-season ahead. The average is the posterior mean of the [REDACTED] win probability, which is the forecast that minimises the expected log-loss penalty.\n\n**How I validated it.** The engine ships without its generator, so I wrote one from the handbook's description (`dev/gen.py`) and produced eleven leagues with exact [REDACTED] win probabilities, seven with guessed hyperparameters and four with hyperparameters matching the real league's estimates. Summed regret over those eleven leagues:\n\n| forecaster | regret sum |\n|---|---|\n| coin flip | 0.2311 |\n| mine | 0.1518 |\n| oracle using the generator's [REDACTED] hyperparameters | 0.1492 |\n\nMy forecaster sits within 2% of the oracle bound for this model class. Along the way I found that freely estimated season covariances cost 15 to 18% regret through sampling noise, which the structured prior fixed. Pooling a second league's moments made things worse, so it is off.\n\n**Operational checks.** Output is byte-identical across repeated runs. A full run on the given league takes about 55 s on two pinned cores with 556 MB peak memory. The program has time guards that cut EM iterations and simulation size if the grader's machine is much slower. Nothing under `engine/` was changed, and the solution only needs `engine`, numpy, pandas and scipy.\n\n**One caveat.** The handbook says the coin flip has almost twice the reference's regret, while on my simulated leagues the coin flip is only 1.4 to 1.6 times my oracle. That could mean the real generator is more predictable than my guess of it, or that the reference is weaker than my oracle. I could not distinguish these without the hidden generator, and a variogram test found no within-season drift signal that a finer time model could exploit."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1228,"cache_read_input_tokens":161475,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1228},"output_tokens":669,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"45d9805e-331d-4ee9-bf4a-c5bbdf92e738","uuid":"26c727b5-0111-4480-b9a5-ddbf27ac9eef","timestamp":"2026-09-25T06:18:23.251Z","request_id":"req_011CfPfsHcf3sTGEk6bz267M"}
